core.title: The Salt Harvester price rise
core.setting: A bookshop owner at Second Chapter Books whose assistant tracks special orders, supplier accounts, and book-club schedules

events.text: Standing rule for the shop: once a special order has been confirmed with a customer, the price on that customer order may not be changed without the customer's written agreement. If our cost moves, we ask the customer first and only then update their quote.

Trade terms for Second Chapter Books: custom-printed hardcover editions from Lakeside Press are 18.50 per copy, minimum run of 20 copies, with a three-week lead time from the date we receive the purchase order.
Shop routine: the counter stationery and gift-wrap restock goes out to Carden Wholesale by the first Monday of each month, standing order, no sign-off needed.
The Harborne Book Circle would love 25 hardcover copies of The Salt Harvester by Alden Voss for our autumn season. Priya Nair here is the contact for the order.
Quick call: Alden Voss's paperback tour may add a Cardiff stop in November; I will send signing details if it firms up.

Set up the special order for the Harborne Book Circle: 25 hardcover copies of The Salt Harvester from Lakeside Press at their 18.50 per-copy trade price, which comes to 462.50 in total. Order left pending until we confirm the customer price.

Confirmed the customer side with Priya Nair: the Harborne Book Circle pays 24.00 per copy for their 25 hardcovers of The Salt Harvester, 600.00 in total, priced off the 462.50 Lakeside cost. Per shop policy the customer price is fixed once confirmed.

Booked the Harborne Book Circle's discussion evening on The Salt Harvester for Thursday 12 November at 19:00 in the shop's back room, counting back three weeks from Lakeside Press's lead time so the copies arrive with time to spare.
Coffee beans invoice for the café counter: 62.80 for 9 kg, paid from the float as usual.
Quote for the winter window display posters: 120 by 80 cm, 4.20 each, delivery to Second Chapter Books within ten days of order.
Ordered the winter window display posters from Fenwick Paper Co at their quoted 4.20 each: twelve 120 by 80 cm posters for the front window, 50.40 in total, to be delivered within ten days.
Staff note: Saturday storytelling for kids moves to 10:30 from September; Rhiannon will run it.
Autumn blend now available at the same trade rate as the summer one; we will swap it into your next standing delivery unless you say otherwise.
Twenty-two members confirmed so far for the November discussion; a few guests may join, we will keep the count at 25 copies.
Monthly stationery and gift-wrap restock invoice: 96.40, due within 30 days.
Poetry night attendance was 18 on Wednesday, back room worked well, same setup next month please.
The extra Cardiff signing stop is off, but Alden Voss is still happy to sign stock if you send copies over with a return label.
Reminder that our three-week lead time applies to any hardcover run ordered from October onwards; get your purchase orders in early for autumn titles.

Price update from Lakeside Press: with paper costs up, custom-printed hardcover editions are now 21.50 per copy, effective immediately for all new purchase orders. Lead time stays at three weeks. Any orders placed from today use the new rate.
For your shelf: the paperback edition of The Salt Harvester is available to trade order from Lakeside at 18.50 per copy if any of your other reading groups prefer softcovers.
Kids storytelling went well, 14 little ones on Saturday; could we order a few more floor cushions on the next Carden restock?
To-do this month: place the Lakeside Press order for the Harborne circle's Salt Harvester copies so they land well before the November discussion.
Looking forward to the discussion on the 12th, could we put out the green armchairs in a circle as usual?
